summary.text: Hakeem Jeffries is the incumbent U.S. Representative for NY-8 and the House Democratic Leader. A Brooklyn native and attorney, he served in the New York State Assembly from 2007 before his election to Congress in 2012, and has led House Democrats since being elected Democratic Leader in November 2022. He is seeking re-election in 2026.

paragraphs.text: Born August 4, 1970, in Brooklyn and raised in the Crown Heights neighborhood; graduated from Midwood High School in 1988.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from SUNY Binghamton (1992), a Master of Public Policy from Georgetown University (1994), and a J.D. from New York University School of Law (1997).

Clerked for U.S. District Judge Harold Baer Jr. in the Southern District of New York, then practiced at the law firm Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison (1998-2004); he also worked at Godosky & Gentile and later served as in-house litigation counsel for Viacom and CBS.

Represented the 57th District in the New York State Assembly beginning in 2007; his Assembly committee assignments included Judiciary, Codes, Correction, Housing and Banks. A 2010 law he sponsored with then-Sen. Eric Adams barred police from compiling the names and addresses of people stopped but not arrested.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2012 and took office in 2013. Early House committee assignments were Judiciary (including its courts, intellectual property and antitrust subcommittees) and Budget.

Elected chair of the House Democratic Caucus in November 2018 (123-113 over Rep. Barbara Lee) for the 116th Congress; his official biography also lists him as a former Whip of the Congressional Black Caucus and former co-chair of the Democratic Policy and Communications Committee.
In January 2020, Speaker Nancy Pelosi named him one of seven House managers for the Senate impeachment trial of President Donald Trump.

His official biography describes him as lead Democratic sponsor of the FIRST STEP Act (signed December 2018), a participant in House passage of the Music Modernization Act (2018), and sponsor of the Keep America's Refuges Operational Act (2018).

Elected House Democratic Leader on November 30, 2022, running unopposed, and re-elected to the post on November 19, 2024; as Democratic Leader he serves on no standing committees. He was Democratic Leader during the 2025 federal government shutdown, which ran from October 1 to November 12, 2025.
